title: Radio on a coin cell
story: A CR2032 coin cell (3.0 V inside, about 15 ohm of internal resistance) powers a tiny radio module. The module needs at least 2.7 V at its pins, and it must draw at least 10 mA to transmit. The resistor in the slot stands for how hard the module works. Pick it.

goals.label: at least 2.7 V reaches the module
the module draws at least 10 mA

hints: Rint (15 ohm) and the module are in series: I = 3.0 / (15 + R).
The module's voltage is 3.0 * R / (R + 15). For 2.7 V you need R of at least 135 ohm.
For 10 mA you need 15 + R of at most 300 ohm, so R of at most 285 ohm.
